candidate.answerReason: The submerged rock adds 1000 cubic centimeters below the surface. Dividing by the 4000-square-centimeter base area gives a rise of 0.25 cm, choice A.

methods.label: Relate displaced volume to a water layer
methods.explanation:
The completely submerged rock occupies \(1000\text{ cm}^3\) below the water surface. The amount of water stays the same, so the volume below the surface must increase by that amount.

The aquarium's base area is
\[
100\cdot40=4000\text{ cm}^2.
\]
A \(1\)-cm rise creates an additional rectangular layer of volume \(4000\text{ cm}^3\). Therefore, the water rises
\[
\frac{1000}{4000}=0.25\text{ cm}.
\]
The resulting depth is \(37+0.25=37.25\) cm, below the \(50\)-cm aquarium height, so no water overflows. The answer is \(\boxed{0.25\text{ cm}}\), choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses rectangular-prism volume and elementary division, with the displacement relationship explained directly.

needsNewNodes.name: Liquid displacement and water-level change
needsNewNodes.description: Relate the volume of a fully submerged solid to the increase in occupied volume below a liquid surface. In a container with constant horizontal cross-sectional area and no overflow, that area multiplied by the level rise equals the submerged solid's volume.
needsNewNodes.reason: The catalog covers prism volumes but lacks the displacement relationship connecting an immersed solid's volume to a liquid-level rise.
